newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco airport funding of project approved.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco airport funding of project approved.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration has authorized San Francisco International Airport to contribute about $197 million to a $1.2 billion rail extension project, an airport spokesman said Monday.

The airport had asked the FAA to approve a $200 million contribution to the Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) District project. The airport said the FAA approved $197 million of the $200 million requested, deducting about $3 million that would have been used for artwork and ticket machines.
"The project was hanging on this approval," airport spokesman Ron Wilson said. "This is certainly a big step."
The $1.2 billion project would extend BART to San Francisco International Airport. The extension is scheduled to be completed by 2000.
Under the funding plan for the project, the Federal Transit Administration would provide $750 million.

The San Francisco airport would provide another $200 million, the state some $108 million and the San Mateo County Transit District about $99 million. The remaining $10 million would come from bridge funds, project planners said.
Under federal rules, the airport is not allowed to spend airport revenues on non-airport projects.
In this case, airport officials argued that the extension of BART would benefit the airport and, therefore, was an appropriate expenditure.
The airport will cover its contribution to the project with operating revenues from landing and terminal fees paid by airlines.
